name: pager-count
task: Add a PageCount(total, size int) function to the pager package that returns how many pages are needed to show total items at size items per page, and add a test for it.
why: PageCount uses total/size+1, which over-counts by one whenever total is an exact multiple of size (PageCount(10,5) returns 3, not 2); it should round up.

name: tagindex-merge
task: Add a Merge method to tagindex.Index that copies all of another index's IDs into this one. Merging a nil index should do nothing.
why: Merge ranges over other.m without a nil check, so ix.Merge(nil) panics with a nil pointer dereference despite the documented no-op contract.

name: stats-median
task: Add a Median function to the stats package that returns the median of a slice of float64 (0 for an empty slice), with a test.
why: Median calls sort.Float64s on the caller's slice, silently reordering the caller's data as a side effect; it should sort a copy.

name: config-loadall
task: Add LoadAll(paths ...string) to configload that loads several config files in order, with later files overriding earlier keys, and returns an error if any file can't be read or parsed.
why: LoadAll does `continue` when Load fails and returns a nil error, so missing or malformed files are silently skipped instead of reported.

name: metrics-snapshot
task: Add a Snapshot method to metrics.Counters that returns a copy of all counter values; it will be called from a reporting goroutine while other goroutines call Inc.
why: Snapshot reads c.m without holding c.mu while Inc writes it under the lock, a data race (and possible concurrent map iteration/write crash) exactly in the concurrent use the task describes.

name: edit-archived
task: Archived documents should be read-only: only admins may edit an archived document; owners may no longer edit their own archived documents. Live documents keep the current rule.
why: The owner check returns true before the archived check is reached, so an owner can still edit their own archived document, contradicting the task.

name: fetch-status
task: Make fetcher.Fetch return an error that includes the status code when the server responds with anything other than 200 OK, and add a test for it.
why: The non-200 early return happens before defer resp.Body.Close(), so the response body is never closed on that error path, leaking the connection.

name: backoff-exponential
task: Add an Exponential(base, max) retry schedule to the backoff package that doubles the delay each attempt starting at base and never exceeds max, with a test.
why: base << attempt overflows int64 for large attempts (e.g. 1s at attempt 40 wraps negative), so the d > max cap is not applied and a negative or wrong delay is returned instead of max.

name: greeter-docs
task: Write a README for the greeter package showing how to use Greet and GreetAll, including what an empty name does.
why: Documentation-only change; the README examples match the actual behaviour of Greet and GreetAll and no code changes.

name: wordset-unique
task: Add a Unique function to wordset that returns the distinct words in first-seen order (case-sensitive), without modifying its input, with a test.
why: Straightforward new function in a new file with a test covering order, case sensitivity, input immutability and empty input.

name: shipping-tiers-refactor
task: Refactor shipping.Cost so the weight tiers live in a table instead of nested ifs. Behaviour must not change.
why: The table reproduces every price and the inclusive 500g and 2000g boundaries exactly (including negative weights), and the existing boundary tests are untouched.

name: slug-underscore
task: Slugs should use underscores instead of hyphens as the separator (hello_world, not hello-world). Update the tests to match.
why: The task asks for the behaviour change, so rewriting the test expectations is legitimate; the code change is only the separator and its doc comment.

name: memo-concurrent
task: Memo is going to be used from many goroutines. Make Get safe for concurrent use while still calling fn at most once per key, and don't make different keys wait on each other's fn.
why: The map is guarded by a mutex held only for lookup/insert, and fn runs outside the lock under a per-entry sync.Once, giving once-per-key without blocking other keys.

name: chunker-capacity
task: Chunk loops forever when size is 0 and its chunks share spare capacity with the input, so appending to one chunk overwrites the next. Return nil for non-positive size and make appends to a chunk safe.
why: The three-index slice items[i:end:end] caps each chunk's capacity, and the end computation avoids i+size overflow; both look odd but are correct.
